environment: Ubuntu 26.04.1 WSL2 x86-64; Docker 29.1.3, cgroup v2, KVM
verification_scope: Two local executions of six scenarios each. Suite acceptance is not approval of intentionally insecure profiles or a claim of healthy guests after OOM/deadline. Reviewed summaries; complete local reports and raw logs are retained outside Git.

expected_outcomes.seccomp-disabled-control: policy rejects unfiltered known guest; clean shutdown follows
expected_outcomes.fd-exhaustion-control: API rejects real file opens; no guest starts; cleanup kills preboot VMM
expected_outcomes.memory-oom-control: host memory cgroup kills VMM; guest is not healthy or gracefully stopped
expected_outcomes.deadline-control: supervisor kills dedicated VM cgroup after budget; no graceful shutdown claim

limits: Trusted helper is privileged and shares the host kernel; no production isolation or escape-resistance claim.
CapBnd remains broad. UTS, IPC, user and cgroup namespaces remain shared with helper.
Seccomp installation was observed, not exhaustive syscall-policy testing.
CPU quota is enlarged only for shutdown; no dedicated CPU reservation. Earlier SIGSEGV/panic remains open.
CPU mitigation findings, guest networking/SSH/egress, I/O/file-size caps, root console and supply-chain limitations remain.

field_notes.report.status: Acceptance of expected scenario outcomes; negative controls are not approved deployments.
field_notes.report.findings: Startup errors only. Console warnings are in scenario.console_findings; earlier failures and panic are retained in jailer-investigation.json.
field_notes.cleanup_forced_stop: Supervisor cleanup had to kill a still-running process. Expected deadline and kernel OOM kills are recorded separately by classification and exit_code.
